scope: Staged independent Session-log queue and exporter ownership

paired.comparison: Actual Source SessionLogReporter and local HTTP collector versus actual Native SessionLogReporter with a controlled exporter port. Compare complete batch payloads/bytes, queue rejection warnings, single-record size refusal, watchdog/stopPending and admission after shutdown.

verification.native: 9 passed: channel corpus, shared flush/shutdown cancellation isolation, failure recovery/independent channels, option/record ownership and direct record/wire regressions.
verification.source: 37 actual channel HTTP cases in this batch; unchanged pinned OTel package 34 tests already passed C8-GE.
verification.scope_reason: Covers the changed channel plus its record/wire providers and meaningful lifetime interleavings without claiming a Native HTTP implementation.

behavior: Queued byte costs include the complete single-record envelope; both count and byte limits trigger draining. Multi-record request selection sums admitted costs without truncating content.
At most one exporter operation runs at once. A processor exportTimeoutMillis warning keeps waiting for settlement before admitting the next request. Failed exports settle and later batches continue.
stopPending discards queued work and its timer while the executing export settles. Shutdown closes emission immediately, drains accepted work and shuts down the exporter once.
Flush/shutdown share stable owned CleanupPromise operations; cancelling a Python waiter does not cancel the owned export. Separate channel instances have independent queues and lifetimes.
Resource/scope and processor options are captured at construction; canonical event content and log attributes are captured at emission.
diagnostics: Initial new tests selected a zero-record fixture as their sample record; fixture selection was corrected before lifecycle assertions.
limitations: The exporter is an explicit internal port; Native HTTP transport, ordinary-event SDK batching, otel service activation and session backend integration remain follow-up work.
Full migration/release, actual Portable/browser and Windows 7 qualification remain pending.
